title: Remove a bit from an unpowered handheld keyless drill
instruction: Remove the drill bit from the unpowered drill and leave the bit in the tray.
context: Carpenters routinely change drill bits while drilling and fastening; this task tests releasing a tool from radial chuck jaws while counterholding the loose drill. Unlike tightening a keyed chuck with its key, a keyless chuck has no key: the bit is freed by twisting the sleeve open by hand against the drill's own body, and the bit is then drawn out and put away.
setup: Three objects on the station counter: a 0.87 kg unpowered battery-removed polymer-housed drill with a steel chuck based on the DCD701 external 185 x 152 x 60 mm envelope lying on its side at x 320 / y 70 mm; a 6 x 93 mm steel round-shank bit (20.64 g) initially retained by three chuck jaws; and a 180 x 120 x 20 mm PP parts tray (100 g) centred at x 320 / y -65 mm. Sleeve diameter 42 mm and internal jaw geometry/forces are estimates. No fixture holds the drill or tray. Initial chuck setting: With battery removed, insert the 6 mm bit 19.0 +/- 0.5 mm past the chuck nose. Counterhold the drill body and turn the sleeve clockwise as viewed from the bit tip, using a low-range torque driver with a nonslip strap adapter, until 0.50 +/- 0.05 N m is reached; hold that torque for 1 s, then remove the reset tool. This is a chosen trial-reset condition, not a manufacturer torque specification. Restore the stated drill and tray poses.
scoring: Score at the end. Every positive tier requires the intact bit wholly outside the finite chuck envelope (42 mm diameter, local axial span 29 to 69 mm in front of the drill origin; 0.15 mm geometric tolerance), independent of drill orientation or which side the bit rests on, the drill supported on the counter with its lowest point within 3 mm of it, the bit supported at counter/tray height with its lowest point between 1 mm below and 25 mm above the counter, both hands released with all four actual pad tips and both midpoints 80 mm clear of every object collider, and under 1 mm motion over 21 samples at 20 Hz for the drill, sleeve, jaws, bit and tray. 0.5: these conditions. 1.0: also the complete bit inside the tray with 5 mm side margins, its lowest surface within 3 mm of the tray floor and its highest surface at most 19 mm above the tray base, with tray tilt at most 5 degrees and its lowest point within 3 mm of the counter. Gentle contact/repositioning is allowed. No opening angle or hidden release flag earns credit.
reset_notes: With battery removed, insert the 6 mm bit 19.0 +/- 0.5 mm past the chuck nose. Counterhold the drill body and turn the sleeve clockwise as viewed from the bit tip, using a low-range torque driver with a nonslip strap adapter, until 0.50 +/- 0.05 N m is reached; hold that torque for 1 s, then remove the reset tool. This is a chosen trial-reset condition, not a manufacturer torque specification. Restore the stated drill and tray poses.
fidelity: Rigid estimated DCD701 shell,0.87kg; passive 3-jaw model:20deg guides,2mm/rev lead,dimensionless sleeve friction0.15,20um interference. Reset real chuck to0.50+/-0.05Nm with19+/-0.5mm insertion; chosen trial condition, not factory spec. Native20um interference is uncalibrated to that torque. Internal geometry/masses/contact estimated; no power,flutes or damage. Finite convex chuck/bit removal test,0.15mm tolerance. Demo uses visible poses/encoders; no attachments or object writes.
scores: Dream-1 run (prior completed recording, regraded with R1 scorer): 0.0; demo (R1): 1.0. Fresh Dream-1 refresh: unscored (authorization error).
